name: Quanta & Kin — Meridian Synth Cuisine Innovation Festival
creator: Meridian Culinary Exchange (MCE), est. 2194
description: A four-day annual food festival held in the Tier 3 Market Arcades and extending into adjacent Tier 2 neighborhoods, celebrating innovation in synthesized, lab-grown, and hydroponic cuisine from chefs and food engineers across all tiers. The festival deliberately spans price brackets — a single admission pass covers both Φ8 synth-dumpling stalls run by the Gray Zone vendors and Φ400 tasting menus from Tier 4 molecular gastronomy labs. Culinary traditions from every human lineage are source material, recombined into dishes that exist nowhere else.
medium: physical attendance, neural-feed taste-documentary broadcast, sensory BCI sample feeds
cultural_impact: Quanta & Kin is one of the few genuinely cross-tier cultural events in Meridian, and its insistence on shared physical space has made it a model for advocates of tiered integration — and a target for those who prefer separation.
controversy: In 2219, a Tier 4 chef submitted a dish that replicated a the Gray Zone grandmother's recipe without credit or compensation, triggering a festival-wide debate about culinary colonialism that resulted in the MCE's mandatory attribution protocols.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone food engineer whose synth-protein recipe won the festival's open category discovers her formula has been quietly patented by a Tier 4 sponsor without her knowledge.

A food critic with a highly influential neural-feed review channel is approached by a corponation to give a negative review of a the Gray Zone vendor who has been organizing labor actions — and the offer is very large.
Someone at the 2226 festival is deliberately poisoning dishes — not lethally, but with a geneware marker that brands the eater's DNA — and no one knows why yet.
